stem:
The diagram shows trapezium $ABCD$ with $AB\parallel DC$. Angle $DAB=70^\circ$. Imran wants angle $ADC$ on the same non-parallel side as angle $DAB$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Angle $ADC=70^\circ$ because angle $ADC$ must equal angle $DAB$ in a trapezium.
Angle $ADC$ cannot be found from the parallel sides alone.
Angle $ADC=110^\circ$ because the angles on the same non-parallel side between the parallel sides add to $180^\circ$.
Angle $ADC=70^\circ$ because $AB$ equals $DC$ on the diagram.

teacher.key_rationale: Co-interior angles between parallel lines on leg AD sum to 180°, so angle ADC=110°. Opposite angles need not be equal in a trapezium. The parallel sides are enough for this pair. AB and DC are not marked equal.
teacher.figure_note: Added trapezium ABCD with AB parallel DC and angle A marked 70°.
